body: Implement bin/watcher.mjs, the [[startup]] daemon per docs/herdr-integration-plan.md section 5.1. Build the pane-to-repo map (herdr api snapshot + herdr worktree list --json + herdr pane process-info), watch .adlc/current-ticket.json, .adlc/manifest.jsonl and the ticket store with fs.watch (writers are atomic-rename), and publish herdr pane report-metadata tokens (ticket = active id from that repo's .adlc/current-ticket.json; phase = the phase of the newest .adlc/manifest.jsonl record for that ticket, token omitted when no record exists) plus workspace-level backlog-count tokens (ready/in-flight/blocked). Read structured ticket data only via the trusted adlc CLI (adlc ticket store export --output <tmp> — the full envelope; `ticket list --json` is a projection WITHOUT completed/edges, verified live) and plain-file reads — never import workspace packages at runtime: the installed plugin is a bare GitHub subdir clone with no node_modules, all with --ttl-ms so stale state self-heals. Publish the mapping as lib/panemap.mjs for the board to reuse. Never call pane report-agent (agent state belongs to herdr built-ins). Fail soft when .adlc/ is absent; malformed JSON yields an explicit unreadable token, never a crash or notification spam. Probe report-metadata rendering and the socket EventMatch subscription; fall back to polling if subscriptions are awkward (plan open questions 1 and 3). All published strings pass lib/sanitize.mjs. Verification: node --test plugins/adlc-herdr/test/watcher.test.mjs with the herdr CLI mocked behind lib/herdr.mjs. allow-suppression: none

edges.contract: t-herdr-2 publishes lib/panemap.mjs (pane-to-repo/ticket mapping) before t-herdr-4 renders it in the board.

title: herdr watcher daemon: .adlc state to per-pane status tokens
